name: Alpha-thalassemia and related disorders

criteria.description: Identification of alpha-globin gene deletions or mutations by molecular genetic testing
Presence of microcytic hypochromic anemia with normal or elevated RBC count
Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing decreased or absent HbA2 and variable HbH or Hb Bart’s depending on subtype
Positive family history of alpha-thalassemia or related hemoglobinopathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular genetic confirmation of alpha-globin gene deletion or mutation plus clinical and hematological evidence of microcytic hypochromic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require combination of genetic testing and hematological studies due to phenotypic variability

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic anemia with low MCV and MCH
searchTerms: anemia with small, light-colored red cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of HbH inclusion bodies in red blood cells
pathognomonic.notes: Detected by supravital staining in HbH disease
searchTerms: red blood cells with HbH inclusions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe intrauterine anemia with hydrops fetalis
pathognomonic.notes: Seen in alpha-thalassemia major (Hb Bart’s hydrops fetalis syndrome)

searchTerms: yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown

common.notes: Enlarged spleen due to extravascular hemolysis

common.symptomName: Bone marrow expansion with frontal bossing
searchTerms: expanded bone marrow causing forehead bulge
fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.notes: Occasionally seen in chronic hemolytic states
Secondary to chronic anemia and marrow expansion

rare.symptomName: Cardiac failure secondary to severe anemia
searchTerms: cardiac problems due to low blood count

rare.symptomName: Extramedullary hematopoiesis causing spinal cord compression
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure from blood cell production outside marrow
spinal cord compression by blood cell masses
sudden severe anemia triggered by infection
temporary bone marrow failure after infection
heart failure due to iron excess

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with normal or elevated RBC count
Low or absent HbA and HbA2 levels on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Presence of HbH or Hb Bart’s hemoglobin depending on genotype
Elevated reticulocyte count in hemolytic forms
Increased serum ferritin and transferrin saturation in iron overload
imaging: Skull X-ray showing bone marrow expansion and 'hair-on-end' appearance
MRI for assessment of iron overload in liver and heart
genetic: Deletion or mutation of one or more alpha-globin genes (HBA1 and HBA2)
Molecular genetic testing confirms diagnosis and subtype
other: Positive family history of alpha-thalassemia or related hemoglobinopathies
Response to hemoglobin H inclusion body staining

distinguishingFeatures: Different pattern of anemia severity and transfusion dependence
Low serum ferritin and iron levels
Presence of abnormal elongated alpha-globin chains

redFlags: Hydrops fetalis with severe anemia in utero
Sudden worsening anemia with aplastic crisis
references: Higgs DR, Engel JD, Stamatoyannopoulos G. Thalassaemia. Lancet. 2012;379(9813):373-383.
